data.name: Pyramid VR
data.detailed_description:
NEW VERSION in the works!

We are completely redesigning the artwork and controls!
This will take some time but we started over, making the art ourselves. Also rewriting all the interactions!
Stay tuned for further updates, once we get a level finished we will add a Beta build for those wanting to test and see the new stuff! Here is a link to a quick art sneak peek!


Nova atualização

Many changes from the start of this project.

Update from Unity 5.5 to Unity 2017.2
Complete Rewrite of the inventory operations
Use right track pad left/right to cycle through inventory
Tutorial now has actual instructions!
Added a map to start game and the jeep is to continue
Better post processing (more vibrant colors, better shadows!)
Added Steam cloud saving
Torch now runs out of fuel
Added 2 full oil cans for the torch (find them!). Just grab and use on torch to 100% refuel
Added another puzzle on lvl2
Refuel small amount of torch oil lighting braziers (Use wisely!)
Added matches to light torch if not close to lit brazier to relight it (Left trigger will auto use a match if you have one)


Please contact us with any concerns! We want the opportunity to resolve any issues before negative reviews!


Acerca do jogo

Remember those days long ago when the idea of gaming was only text?
Those adventure games that drove you nuts, typing in 2 words "go north", "Take Torch" etc...
Frustrating you to no end trying to think of the right combination to just open the freakin door!
Well here it is. The chance to actually FINISH one of those games, in true graphical style!
No more 2 word commands, just point and click your commands! (OK, this was for the PC version, which is now in VR so reach out, grab that item and use it!)
This is a graphical remake of the 1978 Tandy game: Pyramid 2000.
(A tribute to the original style games that started it all)
We tried to stay as true to the text as possible, but due to not having a graphic artist we had to make do with what we could and it is progressing nicely!

Hope to see you at the end!

Christopher/Notso :
  • Team/GDD Creator (This team was great, it all went smooth! thanks guys!)
  • Level/room design
  • Scene decorator...Does this sarcophagus come in pink??
  • Prop Master/funding of the little things required to finish
  • IP rights procurement (License to use music, etc...)
  • Directed and performed VR playtesting.

Alvaro Urrutia Luna
  • Coded extended gameplay features and VR integration.
  • Textured, modeled, and structured levels in a coherent art style.
  • Customized, modeled, and polished scene item game objects.
  • Customized, modeled, and created icons for inventory items.
  • Directed and staged camera and lighting effects.
  • Modified/remodeled Logic and UI for VR.

Thanks to:

Game Engine:
  • Unity, the editor, the team, and the whole community behind it.
Framework:
  • Adventure Creator - ICEBOX Studios
Music:
  • Derek Fietcher - Ancient Egyptian Music - Pharaoh Ramses II
Assets:
  • 3D Everything - Temple of the Pharaoh, Egypt Tomb 2.0
  • Next Level 3D - Ancient Modular Tombs
  • Kiria - Medieval Barrows and Wagons
  • Matias Romero for the great font.
  • Jason Booth - Texture Painter tool
  • Michal - Volumetric Lights
  • VRTK and TheStoneFox for such a great VR Fundations plugin.

We would appreciate a report on the issue instead of a negative rating so we can have a chance to fix the issue. Also please remember that not all Indie games can afford to create their own assets, we did purchase the majority of ours from Unity Asset Store and gave credit to those artists.

3 of us started out on a website called Indieteamup, from 3 different countries. We picked an engine, Unity, a framework, Adventure Creator, and I had the idea for the game. 2 Months later we had a complete game, just needed the set dressing and texturing for release, then along comes the Vive, 2 of us decide to convert it to VR, and here we are. Please enjoy!

This was a non-VR game we developed that we converted to VR, so please be patient as we change everything for room space play!
This is mainly an exploration game with a few minor puzzles and some treasure to collect. Please enjoy!
(This is not in any way meant to be historically accurate so there will be a mix of hieroglyphics and 'god' images unrelated or completely out of context).
The final release we might package the PC version with it as well, until then if interested in the PC demo please see our gamejolt page.

reviews.review:
So my Mom had this bucket list item of seeing the pyramids and I got this to impress her in her first VR experience. This game is jerky, has poor wall recognition where you walk to close to the wall and your VR will go black and the video sometimes glitches/flashes... I have to say that this has/had potential but from the looks of it there are not updates and no real desire to make this a fantastic playable adventure. I had always thought that Nat Geographic should have made a tutorial/exploration game that you could either turn on or off mummys etc... but this is just not a quality game.

My Mom played for about 10 minutes and then with too much walking into blackness and jittery environment her equilibreum finally said enough was enough and she ripped the headset off and said she was going to throw up... it seemed close. Took about 2 hours for her to 'settle down'

Maybe take what you have here as a starting point and try getting funding through kickstarter or indigogo to take it to the next level? This is a homebrew that needs to be fixed... I love the concept, just the programmer(s) didn't have the skill or knowledge to make it consumer friendly. 

I only recommend this to seasoned VR players that can handle poorly written VR gaming at this time...
reviews.developer_response:
Chris: Hard to make updates when no one comes to us with issues, The last note entered 9 days ago clearly says "[b]we are still here if you need any help or to fix any bugs reported.
Please drop us a line with any issues before refunding, give us a chance to make your experience more enjoyable![/b]"
So, yes, we do care.
The blackout is a feature, the fact you get close to a wall and it goes black is what was intended, It prevents you from seeing through walls or other objects, it is not a bug, it then pushes you back to the last good viewable area. That might look like video flashing but it is not. In VR you can't just stop someone's head from going through a wall like in a regular game.
Movement is smooth, very smooth, what hardware are you using? 
I tested this on a core i5 with gtx1060 (if you use lower specs odds are it will not be smooth). Also are you on rift or vive? If using the rift you MUST have roomscale (3 sensors) to prevent tracking loss.
VR sickness is not related to the game, but VR as a whole. We have added the ability to teleport move through the levels, if you played the tutorial level you would see how.
I will be glad to help with any issues, but you have to contact us. 
(With almost 7hrs in this game it can't be that bad...write to us, let us figure out the issues...it does play smooth for well over 300 people}

-----------------------------------------------


Alverik: Hi, bjave. I'm the programmer in this project. Like my team member, I'll start by explaining Headset fading is one of the current standard methods to prevent people seeing through 3d models, be it walls or other objects. This is done to prevent people seeing through walls or seeing the inside of 3d models breaking the immersion (and this is used on most of the objects in our project). The VR developers community is aware it can sometimes be jarring, but this is an issue with the platform, the whole developer community is still learning how to deal with these issues, which are not present in non-VR video games. You'll find this same situation in many other VR titles, it's just more obvious in this project because we use a lot more confined spaces than other titles.

Regarding locomotion, this project is trying to encourage people to get used to touch-pad walking and roomscale physical walking (and as such, it limits the use of teleport). In that regards, I accept it is not a video game for the most novice VR players (and my apologies to your mother). It does take a good while to get used to these kinds of locomotion styles in VR, but it is our belief that VR gaming isn't going to progress until people get past teleport locomotion (and you'll see other game titles already trying to do the same).

Finally, you mentioned National Geographic? We are a two man Indie team, working on our spare time, and the project was never intended to depict the real pyramids in any way. If you've actually read the game's description you'll notice this is a remake of an old Text Adventure (a type of old retro game where there was nothing but textual descriptions in your screen and you had to play by typing word commands into your keyboard). As such, we've never advertised it as a trip to the pyramids, since that is not what it is. My apologies if you misinterpreted the title of the game, unfortunately, we wanted to keep a similar name to the original Text Adventure (Pyramid 2000).

Anyway, if you find any actual bugs feel free to report them and we'll be glad to look into them. Again, my apologies to your mother.
